newsitem.title: TURKEY: Rebel groups kill eight soldiers in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Rebel groups kill eight soldiers in Turkey.

text.p: Kurdish and leftist rebel groups in Turkey killed eight soldiers in separate clashes overnight, state-run Anatolian news agency said on Thursday.
Kurdish rebels in the southeastern province of Siirt killed six soldiers, including one officer, in an ambush using rockets and long-range automatic weapons, the agency said.

In a separate attack, a group of leftist rebels stopped a truck in the Black Sea province of Ordu. They later clashed with security forces arriving at the scene, killing two soldiers and wounding two before escaping, the agency said.

A number of small hardline leftist groups operate in Turkey's remote regions and large cities. Rebels from the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) are fighting for self-rule in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
More than 24,000 people have died in the conflict between the security forces and the PKK, who began their campaign for independence or autonomy in August 1984.
